newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares rise slow, but seen sustained.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares rise slow, but seen sustained.

text.p: Belgian shares continued their sustained rise into record territory on Monday, though dealers noted activity was thin due to London's market holiday.
In the absence of heavy volumes, interest was limited to selected stocks and there was little followthrough buying on the back of Wall Street's strong performance on Friday, they said.
By 0845 GMT, the Bel-20 leading share index .BFX was 3.27 points, or 0.15 percent higher, at 2,257.10 points, a shade off a new record of 2,259.11 set in the first few minutes of trade.

KB Securities technical analyst Francis Smolders said the index was approaching overbought levels but the record breaking run still had some room to run. He put the next resistances at 2,265 and 2,285 points. Supports for the index lay at 2,200 and 2,150 points, he said.
"Indicators are still pointing to higher levels at the moment, but we could get a bit toppish in the next week or two," Smolders said.
Dealers said stocks attracting early interest included cement maker CBR, up 30 francs at 3,595 francs, a shade off its all-time high of 3,600 francs.
One trader put the interest down to speculative buying ahead of the company's annual general meeting on Wednesday, where investors will be looking for news on 1997's trend.
"People are waiting for news (on 1997). It's the same for most cyclicals," one trader said.
He noted chemicals and drugs company UCB was also active on Monday, up 550 francs at 98,200 francs.
